item.title: Full list: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 4
item.description: Como forward Tasos Douvikas has emerged as the top scorer in the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League following the conclusion of Matchday 4 fixtures. The Greek striker moved to the top of the scoring chart after scoring a hat-trick in Como’s emphatic 9-1 victory over Lens on Wednesday. Douvikas has now scored six goals in four appearances in the competition, finding the net in each of Como’s four league-phase matches. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and Club Brugge forward Nicolò Tresoldi are joint-second with five goals apiece. Haaland scored the winning goal in Manchester City’s 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig, while Tresoldi was also on target as Club Brugge defeated PSV Eindhoven 2-1. A further 12 players are tied on four goals, including Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, Barcelona’s Raphinha, Paris Saint-Germain’s Fabián Ruiz and Borussia Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy. Raphinha scored twice in Barcelona’s 3-0 win over Aston Villa, while Ruiz also recorded a brace as PSG thrashed Villarreal 6-0. Meanwhile, Real Madrid’s Mbappé was among the goalscorers in his side’s 3-2 victory over AEK Athens. Below is the list of leading goalscorers after Matchday 4: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 4 6 goals Tasos Douvikas (Como) 5 goals Erling Haaland (Manchester City) Nicolò Tresoldi (Club Brugge) 4 goals Aleksei Batrakov (Galatasaray) Ermedin Demirović (Stuttgart) Serhou Guirassy (Borussia Dortmund) Harry Kane (Bayern Munich) Donyell Malen (Roma) Kylian Mbappé (Real Madrid) Raphinha (Barcelona) Fabián Ruiz (Paris Saint-Germain) Luis Suárez (Sporting CP) Vanguard News The post Full list: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 4 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Abia Commissioner warns journalists against AI-generated fake news
item.description: …Egbu laments media trust deficit, urges fight against quackery By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, has warned journalists against the growing threat of AI-generated fake news, political propaganda and coordinated disinformation campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kanu cautioned that fabricated images, manipulated videos, fake audio recordings and misleading reports could be exploited by political interests to manipulate public opinion, undermine democratic institutions and create electoral tension. He urged journalists to prioritise accuracy and verification over the pressure to break news, insisting that a viral story was not necessarily true. The Commissioner spoke on Wednesday while declaring open the three-day 2026 Media Retreat and Press Week of the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abia State Council, in Umuahia. The retreat, themed “The Future of Journalism in an Era of Disinformation: Preparing Abia Media Practitioners for Democracy and the 2027 Polls,” attracted over 50 media practitioners. Kanu warned journalists against becoming instruments of political manipulation, particularly through fabricated election results, misleading opinion polls, false endorsements and unverified allegations. He challenged correspondents to independently scrutinise government projects rather than rely solely on official statements, urging them to visit project sites, engage beneficiaries and report both achievements and shortcomings. “Where government is doing well, report it. Where there are shortcomings, bring them to public attention. Where explanations are required, demand them. That is the essence of professional journalism,” he said. Speaking also, former Abia Commissioner for Information and columnist, Pastor Ralph Egbu, lamented the growing trust deficit facing journalism, urging correspondents to lead the fight against quackery and defend the profession’s integrity. He stressed that truth and objectivity remained the core ethics of journalism, insisting that practitioners must hold public authorities accountable and use their agenda-setting influence to promote developmental issues. Egbu urged journalists to ask difficult questions and shine the light on society, while discharging their watchdog responsibilities without fear or favour. “There must be a radical commitment to truth and verification,” he declared, challenging journalists to move beyond gatekeeping to community building. He also expressed concern over the damaging influence of artificial intelligence and money on journalism, urging practitioners to guard their integrity, particularly as the 2027 elections approach. Earlier, Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Deacon Steve Oko, said the retreat was designed to equip Abia journalists with the skills and professional capacity required for effective coverage of the 2027 elections. item.title: FinTribe brings women, financial experts together to promote wealth creation
item.description: By Esther Onyegbula Women, financial experts, investment professionals and industry stakeholders converged at the 2026 FinTribe Finance Fair to explore investment opportunities, promote financial literacy and advance women’s participation in wealth creation. The event, organised by FinTribe, brought together representatives of financial institutions, the Nigerian Exchange Group, entrepreneurs and professionals to discuss strategies for building sustainable wealth, managing finances and achieving financial independence. Speaking at the event, founder of FinTribe, Jennifer Awirigwe, said the organisation remained committed to equipping women with the knowledge, confidence and opportunities to make informed financial decisions and build sustainable wealth. She disclosed that the FinTribe community had expanded to include women across 47 countries who had collectively invested more than $8 million. According to her, the organisation had also ventured into real estate, expanded its World Women’s Academy and recently launched a mobile application to connect members with learning resources, investment opportunities and community activities. Awirigwe said: “This movement brings together women across 47 countries who have collectively invested over $8 million. We have built a vibrant community, launched the World Women’s Academy, travelled the world together and created opportunities for women to learn, connect and grow financially. “Recently, we launched our mobile app to bring our community, learning resources, investment opportunities and conversations together in one place.” She explained that the organisation’s impact should be measured by the number of women who had taken practical steps towards financial independence rather than the size of its events. “For me, however, the most important measure of our success is not the number of people in the room. It is the woman who has made her first investment, the woman who has started her business, and the woman who has finally gained the financial confidence to take that important step,” she said. Speaking on the theme of the fair, ‘I CAN’, Awirigwe said it was designed to challenge limiting beliefs that prevent women from pursuing financial opportunities, owning property and building generational wealth. She urged participants to take advantage of the financial experts and investment professionals at the event, engage with exhibitors, ask questions and translate the knowledge acquired into practical financial decisions. In his remarks, Chief Executive Officer of NGX Regulation Limited, Mr Olufemi Shobajo, commended FinTribe for sustaining conversations around financial inclusion, investor education and the development of Nigeria’s financial ecosystem. item.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) that fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled: “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” stated: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance. Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorized. If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. “To safeguard port integrity and vessel safety, all maritime operators, terminal users, and personnel must utilise authorised reporting protocols immediately upon detecting any security incident or anomaly,” the agency stated. item.title: Race For 2028 Heats Up After US Midterms Firestorm
item.description: President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama. Supporters cheer as Democrat senatorial candidate Roy Cooper speaks during an election night event in Raleigh, North Carolina on November 3, 2026. Republicans In Turmoil The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb. Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterm campaigns with rallies in swing states. The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday. But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump. Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico celebrates with supporters after winning the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden. “The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations said. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about. Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms, but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war. The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal. He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning Senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state. item.title: GNI overhauls claims operations, clears N3bn claims
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze In a decisive move to reclaim its market position and confidence, Great Nigeria Insurance Plc, GNI, has undertaken a comprehensive overhaul of its claims operations, clearing over N3 billion in claims. According to the company, the liquidation of these liabilities marks one of the most aggressive debt-clearing exercises in the company’s recent history, signaling a clean break from operational bottlenecks. Recognizing that prompt claims settlement remains the primary test of an insurer’s value proposition, GNI’s Executive Management placed its priority on financial restructuring to address long-standing obligations. Having reconstituted its board of Directors and Executive Management, GNI Plc took a bold resolution to confront structural and systemic challenges undermining its operations over the years. At the epicenter of these challenges is the accumulation of outstanding claims that had severely tarnished customer confidence and strained relationships with key industry stakeholders.The organization therefore, placed immediate claims settlement at the core of its corporate turnaround strategy. Meanwhile, GNI hosted two strategic brokers’ fora themed “GNI Reloaded” in Ibadan and Lagos to formalize this operational shift and rebuild crucial trade channels, given that insurance brokers facilitate a significant percentage of commercial and institutional policies in Nigeria. GNI stated: “To prevent future backlogs and ensure long-term operational efficiency, GNI’s Executive Management has instituted a maximum 48-hour Turnaround Time (TAT) window for processing and paying verified claims. Under this new service level agreement (SLA), once a claim is documented and verified by adjusters, payment authorization must occur within 48 hours.” Management emphasizes that this policy is not merely a promotional promise, but an embedded operational mandate backed by streamlined digital workflows and revamped internal approval controls. “By combining substantial capital deployment with structural service delivery reforms, Great Nigeria Insurance Plc aims to position itself as a reliable and responsive player in Nigeria’s evolving financial services sector.” The post GNI overhauls claims operations, clears N3bn claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FDI: Qatar’s Barzan Holdings seeks to deepen defense partnerships with Nigeria
item.description: By Tunde Oso Barzan Holdings, Qatar’s leading national defence and security company, has spotlighted its cutting-edge defence technologies and industrial capabilities at the 2026 Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX), held in Lagos, as part of efforts to advance defence innovation, strengthen industry collaboration and support Nigeria’s evolving security needs. As one of the sponsors of the exhibition, Barzan Holdings engaged with Nigerian defence stakeholders to explore commercial, technological and industrial collaborations across its four business sectors: weapons and ammunition; advanced technology; platforms; and services, support and accessories. Beyond equipment supply, the company offers capabilities across the defence lifecycle, including training, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), and technical support. Its portfolio includes unmanned surface vessels and unmanned aerial vehicles for surveillance and intelligence missions, as well as command-and-control systems designed to enhance situational awareness and support operational decision-making. The event also served as an avenue to showcased the company’s weapons portfolio, which include the Q1 Corner rifle and the recently launched BIG556 rifles in 4.5-inch and 7-inch configurations, designed and manufactured in Qatar. Speaking during the exhibition, the Regional General Manager for Africa at Barzan Holdings and Managing Director of DICON-SUR, Engineer Thamer Al Emadi, said the event provided an important platform to engage with key defence stakeholders, demonstrate the company’s technological capabilities and identify areas of collaboration aligned with Nigeria’s defence priorities. He stated: “We are here at AFRIDEX to discuss Nigeria’s defence needs and explore how Barzan Holdings can support them through the supply of modern defence products and services, as well as potential industrial and technology partnerships. ‘‘We are open to developing solutions that address the specific requirements of the Nigerian Defence Forces and contribute to strengthening the country’s sovereign security.” The post FDI: Qatar’s Barzan Holdings seeks to deepen defense partnerships with Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s economy sustains growth as PMI rises to 53.2 points
item.description: •Industry, agriculture strengthen expansion; services growth slows By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Nigeria’s economy sustained its growth momentum in October 2026, with the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 53.2 points from 53.0 points in September, indicating a fifth consecutive month of expansion in economic activities. The latest PMI report released by the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, yesterday, showed that growth was recorded across the three major sectors of the economy — Industry, Services and Agriculture — although the pace of expansion varied, with Agriculture maintaining its position as the best-performing sector. The report indicated that 24 of the 32 subsectors surveyed expanded during the review month, while eight contracted, pointing to a broad-based improvement in business activities. A breakdown of the sectoral performance showed that the Industry PMI rose to 52.6 points in October from 52.0 points in September, representing a third consecutive month of expansion in industrial activities. Of the 16 industrial subsectors surveyed, 12 recorded expansion, while four contracted. Similarly, the Agriculture PMI increased significantly to 54.7 points from 53.1 points in September, extending the sector’s uninterrupted expansion streak to 27 months. All five agricultural subsectors surveyed recorded growth during the period, making agriculture the strongest-performing sector in the economy. Livestock recorded the highest PMI at 56.4 points, while Agricultural Support Services recorded the lowest at 52.0 points. General Farming Activities, New Orders, Employment and Inventories remained in expansion, at 56.8, 55.6, 52.9 and 53.6 points, respectively However, the Services sector recorded a marginal moderation in growth, as its PMI declined to 52.7 points in October from 53.2 points in September. Despite the decline, the sector sustained its expansion for the fourth consecutive month, with seven of the 11 subsectors surveyed recording growth, while four contracted. Further analysis of the report showed improvements in key indicators of economic activity, including output, new orders, employment and raw materials inventory. The Output Index rose to 53.5 points in October, while the New Orders and Employment indices increased to 52.1 points and 52.7 points, respectively. The Raw Materials Inventory Index also improved to 51.8 points from 51.1 points in September, remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. The improvement in new orders and employment suggests that businesses experienced increased demand and continued to expand their workforce during the review period. However, businesses continued to contend with rising costs, as the Composite Input Price Index increased by 0.7 points, while the Output Price Index rose by 0.5 points. item.title: ‘Tinubu’s Educational Reforms Have Returned Over One Million Children To Classrooms’
item.description: President Bola Tinubu’s reforms in the education sector since he assumed office have returned over one million out-of-school children to learning. The development was revealed in a statement by the APC Presidential Campaign Council Spokesperson, Dele Alake, on Wednesday, saying that the reforms have also expanded access to learning, improved teachers’ welfare, and stabilised the academic calendar across higher institutions in the country. Quoting the Federal Ministry of Education through its Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) 2026 report, Alake noted that the government’s interventions cover basic and secondary education, technical and vocational training, and tertiary education. He explained that the reforms focus on six priority areas: technical and vocational education, science and medical sciences, out-of-school children, girl-child education, digitalisation and education quality assurance. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. Increased Funding For Basic Education According to the NESRI report, Alake explained that the Federal Government allocated a record ₦3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget and secured $552 million for the HOPE-EDU programme, which targets 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools. The report said the BESDA programme has returned over one million out-of-school children to learning, trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and established 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states. It added that the AGILE programme has reached 7.19 million girls, with 3.7 million enrolled in secondary schools, while over 10,000 schools have benefited from improved facilities. FILE PHOTO: A classroom at PAMO University. Credit: PAMO University of Medical Sciences Curriculum Reform And Teacher Development The NESRI index indicated that the administration has introduced a revised national curriculum that reintroduces Nigerian History and strengthens Civic and Heritage Studies. For instance, the National Learning Assessment has been restored to monitor pupils’ performance and identify learning gaps. Under EduRevamp, Alake noted that a total of 53,553 teachers have registered, while 51,794 joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP), a six-month programme offering professional qualifications, certification and licensing. Backed by ₦2 billion, the programme targets 250,000 teachers by 2027. Also, Alake, who doubles as the Minister for Solid Mines and Minerals, explained that the Inspire Live initiative provides online lessons from Primary One to Senior Secondary School Three, supported by certified teachers and AI-assisted learning. Dele Alake TVET Programme Records Over 156,000 Beneficiaries Under President Tinubu’s administration, Alake noted that the TVET scheme has attracted over 2.8 million applications, with 156,446 verified trainees receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support. item.title: FG records N4.69trn fiscal deficit in Q1’26 as revenue falls
item.description: Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% – Budget Office By Udeme Akpan The Federal Government (FG) recorded an aggregate fiscal deficit of N4.69 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, as revenue generation fell significantly below target, highlighting challenges in financing the 2026 budget. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% On economic performance, the Budget Office reported that the oil sector grew by 2.57 per cent year-on-year in real terms during the first quarter, up by 0.70 percentage points from 1.87 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The non-oil sector expanded by 3.94 per cent, outperforming the oil sector and accounting for a larger share of the economy’s growth. The Budget Office described the performance as “a period of macroeconomic stabilisation accompanied by moderate real-sector expansion.” However, it identified weak, although improving, revenue performance as a major constraint to budget execution, noting that the Federal Government continued to meet its non-discretionary expenditure obligations. It stated: “Improving revenue collections in the subsequent quarters of the year is critical to the successful execution of the 2026 Budget.” The report said the government would intensify efforts to improve economic growth and revenue generation, while controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs. This development, stakeholders said, has introduced a new dimension into the evolving political configuration of the state and the wider Niger Delta ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, he cautioned that “the success of any political platform must depend on its policies, credibility and commitment to the people’s welfare, not merely political structures or personalities.” Cultural Renaissance, Political Symbolism The traditional boat regatta at Toru-Orua, according to Okaba, underscored the importance of Ijaw cultural identity in political engagement. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 5, 2026
item.description: The naira is trading at different rates against the US dollar across Nigeria’s official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the dollar is valued at approximately ₦1,347.30, based on the latest reported official rate. At the parallel market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators are buying the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 and selling at ₦1,390. The figures indicate that Nigerians buying dollars through the parallel market are paying more than those accessing foreign exchange through the official window. The difference between the official rate and the parallel market selling rate is approximately ₦42.70 per dollar. Exchange rates fluctuate depending on dollar supply, demand, market liquidity and trading activities. The parallel market rate may also vary across locations and individual currency dealers. Nigerians seeking foreign exchange for international travel, school fees, business transactions and other payments are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed Bureau De Change operators before completing transactions. item.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, other candidates
item.description: …Governor highlights projects, promises more roads, jobs, infrastructure …Charges electorate to sweep away opposition with their votes The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State on Wednesday officially flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders and stakeholders pledging to mobilise voters across the state for the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu. The campaign flag-off, which held at Nsukka Township Stadium, witnessed a large turnout of party faithful, political office holders, traditional and community leaders, as well as supporters from across the three senatorial districts. Speakers at the event described the mammoth crowd as a demonstration of the APC’s political strength in Enugu State, insisting that the party was determined to consolidate its presence and secure victory for all its candidates in the forthcoming elections. Addressing the gathering, Governor Mbah highlighted his administration’s investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, and revival of moribund assets and completion of abandoned projects. He urged the people to assess his government’s performance through its achievements and ongoing projects, noting that the opposition had not even presented any manifesto. Reflecting on his journey to Nsukka ahead of the rally, Mbah said the ongoing dualisation of the Penoks–T-Junction – Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road had significantly reduced travel time and improved safety. “I left the office a few minutes past 1pm. It took me two to three minutes to get to T-Junction from Penoks. And it just reminded me of how motorists could have spent so much time, sometimes up to 30 minutes or hours if we did not dualise that road. “From T-Junction all the way to Nsukka, I noticed that work was going on right left, green, what have you. The contractor assured me that a realistic commissioning date is before the end of this year. “Another thing the road reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. Once upon a time, we dreaded traveling on that road because of fear of attack are gone. Today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he stated. According to him, the administration’s infrastructure programme is not merely about constructing roads, but also about reconnecting communities, expanding economic opportunities and promoting greater integration across the state. He cited the 40km Owo-Ubahu-Amankanu-Umualor-Ikem virgin dual carriageway, which connects to Obollo-Afor road as another intervention designed to improve connectivity, and now links communities in the northern part of the state, while also serving as a new gateway to the North Central part of the country. item.title: APC has mechanism to manage our govs, Rainbow Coalition’s feud — Yilwatda
item.description: *We’ve no plan to make Nigeria one party state *Nigerians should choose leaders based on records, character, capacity to deliver *Says Tinubu’s reforms must translate into jobs, food, better incomes, security By Soni Daniel, Northern Regional Editor National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said the ruling party has no ambition to turn Nigeria into a one-party state despite the influx of politicians from opposition parties into its fold. Yilwatda, who spoke on the 2027 general elections, governance and the APC’s preparations for the polls, said a strong ruling party and a competitive multiparty democracy could coexist. In an interview with Vanguard, the APC chairman also said the party had mechanisms to resolve differences between some APC governors and the Federal Capital Territory Minister, Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, insisting that internal disagreements would not derail its preparations for the elections. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the administration had established measures to reposition the economy but must now translate them into jobs, affordable food, better incomes and improved security. Yilwatda urged Nigerians to assess candidates on their records, character and capacity to deliver rather than allow political differences to dictate their choices. As a democrat, are you not worried that the mass exodus of other politicians into the ruling APC can create a one-party state if the APC wins in January next year? I am a democrat, and I believe that Nigeria’s democracy is stronger when political parties are vibrant, competitive and able to offer citizens credible alternatives. The APC does not seek to eliminate opposition, nor do we believe that a healthy democracy can be sustained without it. The movement of politicians from one party to another is a feature of democratic politics. Individuals make such decisions for different reasons, and every Nigerian has the constitutional right to freedom of association. What matters is that these movements are voluntary and conducted in accordance with the law. However, the responsibility for maintaining a competitive political environment does not rest with the APC alone. Opposition parties must also strengthen their internal structures, build public confidence, articulate credible policies and organise effectively. Our ambition is not to turn Nigeria into a one-party state. Our ambition is to build a party that Nigerians freely choose because of its leadership, programmes and record of performance. item.title: ‘How BVN exposed fake Amnesty beneficiaries’
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA—The Presidential Amnesty Programme, PAP, has said its insistence on the Federal Government’s Bank Verification Number, BVN, policy has exposed fake beneficiaries and fraudsters feeding off the programme. The office, while condemning what it described as blackmail and campaign of calumny against its administrator, Dr. Dennis Otuaro, by some misguided elements from the Niger Delta, said it would not succumb to blackmail and will not sideline the BVN policy designed to link all bank accounts belonging to individuals and eradicate corruption. “The PAP office cannot be the exception in the execution of the government’s policy on BVN designed to eradicate corruption in the society,” the Office said in a statement, yesterday, Mr. Igoniko Oduma, Special Assistant on Media to the Administrator, said. “Clearly, anybody using the tool of blackmail to arm-twist the office to sideline BVN is either a criminal or a fraudster, who should be under security watch. The Office has asked them to come for verification of their claims, but they will not. “These serial blackmailers are purveyors of falsehood and hollow narratives; they are driven by sheer greed with the sole objective of denting Dr. Otuaro’s image and distracting him from focusing on the task given to him by President Bola Tinubu. “These misguided elements are angry with Dr. Otuaro for prudent management of resources, and introducing reforms that have sanitised the PAP. Many of them are angered by what is statutorily paid to them by the Office. Some want to be awarded bogus contracts which, the office under Otuaro, is not inclined to do.” The programme said rather than divert funds to satisfy blackmailers, resources are being deployed efficiently for lasting peace and security in the Niger Delta, with tangible results including 13,300 onshore and over 500 offshore scholarships, distribution of laptops to beneficiaries, and prompt payment of ex-agitators’ monthly stipends. It listed other achievements as employment of four cadet pilots and 20 aviation trainees after training, on-the-job training for 40 cadets, professional certification for 98 maritime cadets, and training of over 360 stakeholders on alternative dispute resolution and mediation. item.title: VIDEO: Makinde Unveils Manifesto, Faults Nigerian Leaders For Lack Of Ideas
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed Nigeria’s development challenges on a lack of ideas among its leaders, despite the country’s vast natural and human resources. Makinde made the remarks on Wednesday in Abuja during the unveiling of his manifesto for the 2027 general elections. The Oyo State Governor said the document outlines his proposed solutions to the country’s economic, political, social and institutional challenges. He explained that the manifesto was drawn up after extensive consultations with Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones, including town hall meetings where participants shared their expectations for the country. item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. “I enumerated some of the promises I made to Nigerians. One of the promises is to make sure that security is restored in every part of this country.” ﻿ Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election.
